Meet The Speakers

Some text here

Dimitris Galanis

Dimitris Galanis holds a Ph.D. in Natural Language Processing (Nov. 2006 – Feb. 2012, title: “Automatic Generation of Natural Language Summaries”), an M.Sc. in Computer Science and a B.Sc. in Informatics. All the aforementioned degrees were obtained in the Department of Informatics at Athens University of Economics and Business.

Stergios Chatzikyriakidis

Stergios Chatzikyriakidis is Professor of Computational Linguistics at the Department of Philology, University of Crete, where he directs the Computational Linguistics and Language Technology Lab. He is also Head of Research at MuVeS AI and founder of SimasiaAI. His work lies at the intersection of NLP, formal semantics and type theory, the reasoning and evaluation of large language models, Computatonal Dialectology and low-resource varieties. He holds an MSc and a PhD from King’s College London.

Prokopis Prokipidis

Prokopis Prokopidis is a researcher and computational linguist at the Institute for Language and Speech Processing (ILSP) / Athena RC, where he has worked since 1998. He holds a degree in English Language and Literature from the University of Athens and an MA in Computational Linguistics from the University of Essex. He has participated in Greek and European projects focused on natural language processing, information extraction, and language resource development. He has contributed to the creation of annotated corpora, such as the Greek Dependency Treebank, as well as tools for automatic text annotation. His recent research includes named-entity recognition for archaeological texts, anonymization for court decisions, and the development of evaluation resources for Greek large language models. He has published in conferences, journals, and edited volumes.

Stella Markantonatou

Dr. Stella Markantonatou holds an MA in Chemical Engineering (NTUA 1983), BA in Linguistics (NKUA 1988) and a PhD in Linguistics (University of Essex 1992). She is an Emeritus Research Director at the Institute for Language and Speech Processing/ATHENA RC and a Principal Researcher in the AI Unit Archimedes/ATHENA RC. Her expertise lies in NLP for under-resourced language varieties with a focus on Modern Greek dialects and idiomatic speech, in language resource development and in knowledge representation.

Vassilis Gatos

Basilis G. Gatos received his Electrical Engineering Diploma and Ph.D. degree in Optical Character Recognition Techniques from the Democritus University of Thrace, Greece. He currently serves as a Researcher at the Institute of Informatics and Telecommunications of NCSR “Demokritos” in Athens, Greece, and is a co-founder of the spin-off companies AI4Doc and Astros Intelligence. His professional career spans leadership roles in R&D at Lambrakis Press Archives, Computer Logic S.A., and BSI S.A. With research interests focused on Image Processing, Document Image Analysis, OCR, and Pattern Recognition, Dr. Gatos has authored over 200 publications in international journals and conference proceedings and participated in numerous EU-funded research programs. A member of the Technical Chamber of Greece, he regularly serves on program committees for major international conferences (such as ICDAR, ICFHR, and DAS) and co-organized ICFHR 2014, DAS 2016, and ICDAR 2024 in Greece.

Kanella Pouli

Kanella Pouli holds a BSc in Linguistics from the University of Athens and an MSc in Language Technology from the University of Athens and the National Technical University of Athens. She has been a Scientific Associate at ILSP/Athena RC since 2012 and has contributed to the following European and national projects: QTLaunchPad, CEF-ELRC, FutureTDM, ELRC+L2, CRACKER, ISD, CLARIN:EL, Apollonis, ELE, LDS, LLMs4EU, and AltEdic4EU.
